comments.body: Former user, Jared Whiklo, Diego Pino Navarro, Nick Ruest are you folks making use of the org.fcrepo.jms.properties header with any of your camel code? This ticket is about making that header go away (a good idea IMO, especially since the data it carries is not accurate). Will the Islandora CLAW code have any issues with that?

Unknown, i think we don't (but will check tomorrow AM to be sure) : the only part where we interact with org.fcrepo.jms is here https://github.com/Islandora-CLAW/CLAW/blob/252fc35433aef32fef0ac7966182fb3ad491cea6/camel/sync/src/main/resources/OSGI-INF/blueprint/eventGateway.xml
and if i remember well we fetch data from fedora directly, first hand, instead of depending on that header, we just use the event type, not the properties.
Thanks!

It looks like the fcrepo-audit-triplestore camel code uses the org.fcrepo.jms.properties header value: https://git.io/vasaR

Andrew Woods does that imply that the JMS module should continue to publish these events? And if so, is there an expectation that the listed properties are only those that directly operated on (the current behavior) or those that changed in the internal representation (much harder)?

Unknown at fcrepo-audit-triplestore org.fcrepo.jms.properties is used basically only for getting the premisType right? https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-audit/blob/master/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/audit/AuditUtils.java#L64-L91

Maybe we can refactor that utility function by getting needed info from fedora directly? too much overhead?
+1 to going back to the repo for that info.

It would not be possible to go back to the repo for DELETE events, since the information will no longer be there.

My understanding, though, is that if the JMS event simply announced whether the affected resource was a Container or a Binary, that would be enough for the audit system – it would also make things easier for some of the other camel routes.
What about indexing? Is it possible to do deindexing of deleted things without the props?
Indexing (and deindexing) works just fine now without the props.
SO why would we need to go back to the repo for DELETEs for audit?

The difference is that in the indexing context, a DELETE event simply removes all trace of that resource in the external index, which doesn't require any interaction with the repository. For audit, however, the camel route is recording that a DELETE event happened, and if the fedora:hasContent property exists in the properties header (as it does for any fedora:Binary resource – whether the binary itself changes or the metadata describing that binary). If the fedora:hasContent property is present, then the premis:hasEventType is set as http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/audit#contentRemoval; otherwise, the premis:hasEventType is http://id.loc.gov/vocabulary/preservation/eventType/del.

In some ways, though, this is orthogonal to the discussion of properties, since the only value in question is fedora:hasContent, which is specially added to any fedora:Binary, regardless of the properties that may or may not be changed. In fact, I would assert that fedora:hasContent is not a property like any of the other values packed into that header. It is certainly not one that has been changed.

If we need to retain this sort of functionality for the audit stream, I think a better solution would be to not publish properties at all but rather publish whether the object is a Container or a Binary, along the lines of the HTTP Link headers that are currently published for every resource.
We don't need any further info for DELETEs. I wonder about MOVES in this context. Are they handled as delete + create?
Yes, I would think that publishing the types of a resource should be enough.

See this for background on MOVE events: https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1937

The behavior in master now is that a MOVE operation emits a MOVE event for the resource in question (and all of its children) and a DELETE event for the resource's previous location (and the previous location of all children).
Do we have a conclusion for this that types are enough in the events?
Unknown I can confirm, i did not find any use at islandora for org.fcrepo.jms.properties, so we are good to go at our side. Thanks and sorry for the delayed response.
The types thing doesn't work: you can't get the types of a deleted node. Thoughts?

Not necessarily an ideal solution, but look here: https://git.io/varCm

If, e.g. Event::getPath contains JCR_CONTENT, we know it is (was) a fedora:Binary; otherwise, it was a fedora:Container. Would that work?
What about other types? I don't think that is nearly complete enough.

I agree. If we are going to list RDF:type values, it should be complete.

What about optionally Inject}}ing an eventBus to {{FedoraResourceImpl and if it's nonnull, adding a FedoraEvent directly to it here: https://git.io/var2N

That would allow us to call FedoraResource::getTypes before the object is removed. That may also mean filtering out any JCR-based REMOVE events in the DefaultFilter.

OK, I have a much better approach: take a look at this function: https://git.io/vaocq

By casting to a org.modeshape.jcr.api.observation.Event, you can call getMixinTypes() on the Event, which will include any RDF type added to the resource (I have confirmed this via logging statements). This will not include the LDP types, but those are dynamically added based on the Fedora types anyway and aren't part of the FedoraResource::getTypes response (a bug?). See: https://git.io/vaocw

Specifically, with this addition to the DefaultFilter:

         try {
             final org.modeshape.jcr.api.observation.Event modeEvent =
                     (org.modeshape.jcr.api.observation.Event) event;
+            // ----------------------------------------------
+            LOGGER.info("Event Type: {}", modeEvent.getType());
+            LOGGER.info("Event Path: {}", modeEvent.getPath());
+            LOGGER.info("Primary Type: {}", modeEvent.getPrimaryNodeType().toString());
+            stream(modeEvent.getMixinNodeTypes()).map(NodeType::toString).forEach(type ->
+                    LOGGER.info("Mixin Type: {}", type));
+            // ----------------------------------------------
+
             return concat(of(modeEvent.getPrimaryNodeType()), stream(modeEvent.getMixinNodeTypes()))
                 .map(NodeType::toString);
         } catch (final ClassCastException e) {

INFO 20:53:43.080 (DefaultFilter) Event Path: /events/test1
INFO 20:53:43.080 (DefaultFilter) Primary Type: nt:folder
INFO 20:53:43.080 (DefaultFilter) Mixin Type: fedora:Resource
INFO 20:53:43.080 (DefaultFilter) Mixin Type: fedora:Container
INFO 20:53:43.080 (DefaultFilter) Mixin Type: ex:Object

Note the presence of ex:Object in the output.
Very cute. One question: if the action that triggers the event is "a type is removed", is it included in the list of types, or not?
I would think that the removed type would not be included in that list. What do you think?

I don't know-- that's why I raised the question.

{grin}

I guess I'm wondering how it plays into the audit use case. There's no way within the API that one could switch a container to anything else or anything else into a container. Is that the only edge case? I think it might be.

It wouldn't affect the audit case, since for the audit system, the only relevant types are fedora:Container and fedora:Binary. And it is not possible to change those types through the public HTTP APIs.
